scenarios.title: Repair a credential policy
scenarios.summary: Repair the staff sign-in policy while keeping legitimate staff access available.
scenarios.objective: Reject the short and listed proposals. Keep the supplied new staff phrase eligible. Require a replacement after confirmed compromise. Require the valid password and bound authenticator proof. Accept both supported device proof methods and reject the incomplete sign-in trials.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Compare the required case with the current outcome, adjust the policy and try again.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: A minimum length sets the shortest acceptable password. A separate list blocks common or compromised passwords. An entry can meet the length requirement and still be on the list. Evaluate the proposal when setting or changing the password.

guide.title: Try the separate example
guide.why: Knowing the existing password can still produce a match after it has been exposed. When a compromise is confirmed, require an approved replacement before allowing normal sign-in.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: A password and a memorized code are both things a person knows. A device can prove that it holds a private key. A public certificate can help identify that key; presenting the certificate alone proves no possession. A local biometric can unlock the bound device, which then supplies the key proof. Some systems use a device-based authenticator instead of a password. This activity keeps the password and adds a second factor.

scenarios.explanation: The local policy separates length and list checks for new passwords from sign-in and compromise response. It accepts the two verified key proofs and requires a distinct possession factor in addition to the password.
hints: Compare the two unlisted proposals to choose a threshold that separates them.
A list check can reject a long password. Replacement concerns a different trial, where the current password still matches.
Check actual possession evidence. Two memorized values and a copy of a public certificate are insufficient.
scenarios.simplifications: The virtual policy reads lengths, list membership, a compromise flag, and supplied verification outcomes. It stores no secrets and implements no authenticator, password recovery, cryptography, or biometric capture. The stated minimums are local lab cases. Other password composition and passwordless policies are outside this simulation.

scenarios.title: Choose a suitable VPN design
scenarios.summary: Repair the virtual VPN policies for a branch LAN and an individual remote device.
scenarios.objective: Protect exchanges between the full branch and office LANs with the two gateways. Protect the individual remote device’s traffic to the listed office service range only. Apply both profiles and verify the reverse direction, the adjacent excluded service, and ordinary same-LAN traffic.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Compare the required case with the current outcome, adjust the policy and try again.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: A site-to-site design joins two networks through their security gateways. Remote access connects one remote device to an office gateway. Use the role of each participant to decide which device handles the tunnel.

guide.title: Try the separate example
guide.why: The outer addresses identify the tunnel endpoints. The inner addresses identify the original source and destination. A gateway can protect an entire LAN. One remote client can have a single assigned inner address, written as a /32 prefix.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: Match the prefixes on both sides. A remote device may need only one office service range. Use a trial just beyond that range and a normal same-LAN trial to verify the policy leaves those paths alone.

scenarios.explanation: The site profile protects exchange between the complete LANs. The remote profile protects the one supplied client address and the restricted office service range. The tunnel endpoint roles and both address ranges must agree.
hints: Read the outer addresses as endpoint facts. Edit the inner ranges to decide which original addresses use a profile.
Permit the assigned remote device with /32. Use the supplied service range for the other side.
When a profile changes, apply it before comparing actual traffic to the requirements.
scenarios.simplifications: Offline teaching model of IPsec endpoint roles and bidirectional IPv4 traffic selection. It configures neither actual IPsec nor VPN interfaces, routing, packet processing, authentication, algorithms, security associations, or negotiation.
